meta.title: HSK 1 content set
meta.source: Lesson order follows HSK Standard Course 1 (HSK标准教程 1, 15 lessons). All words on the official HSK 1 list are included; textbook extras are marked official_hsk1=false.
notes: Example sentences are original, built from HSK 1 words; they are not copied from the textbook.
Pinyin is given in dictionary form: neutral tones unmarked, tone changes of 不 and 一 written as they are said, two-3rd-tone changes not written.
Stroke counts, radicals and decompositions come from Make Me a Hanzi (github.com/skishore/makemeahanzi).

patterns.name: Greetings with 好
patterns.explanation: Add 好 after a person to greet them. 您好 is the polite form.

patterns.name: Apologising
patterns.explanation: 对不起 says sorry; 没关系 is the usual answer.

patterns.name: Thanking and goodbye
patterns.structure: 谢谢 → 不客气 ; 再见
patterns.explanation: 谢谢 is answered with 不客气. 再见 means goodbye.

patterns.name: Negation with 不
patterns.explanation: 不 goes before the verb or adjective to make it negative. Before a 4th-tone syllable 不 is read bú.

patterns.name: Saying your name with 叫
patterns.explanation: 叫 means 'to be called'. Ask with 你叫什么名字？

patterns.name: 'A is B' with 是
patterns.structure: A + 是 + B ; A + 不是 + B
patterns.explanation: 是 links two nouns. It is not used before adjectives.

patterns.name: Yes/no questions with 吗
patterns.explanation: Put 吗 at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question. Word order does not change.

patterns.name: Question words 谁 and 哪
patterns.explanation: Question words sit where the answer will go. No 吗 is needed.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de Hànyǔ lǎoshī.

patterns.name: Possession with 的
patterns.explanation: 的 works like 's. With close people or a family, 的 is often dropped: 我妈妈, 我家.

patterns.name: 'And you?' with 呢
patterns.explanation: 呢 after a noun asks the same question again about that person or thing.

examples.english: I'll have tea, how about you?

patterns.name: Asking 'how many' with 几
patterns.explanation: 几 asks about small numbers (usually under 10) and needs a measure word.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén?
examples.english: How many people are in your family?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu sān kǒu rén.
examples.english: There are three people in my family.
How many friends do you have?

patterns.name: Asking age
patterns.structure: 你几岁了？ ; 你多大了？
patterns.explanation: Use 几岁 for children and 多大 for adults. 了 marks the new age reached.

patterns.name: Numbers up to 100
patterns.explanation: Build numbers from 一 to 十: tens first, then units.

patterns.name: Can (learned skill) with 会
patterns.explanation: 会 means you have learned how to do something.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú huì xiě zhège zì.

patterns.name: Adjective sentences with 很
patterns.explanation: Adjectives act as the verb. 是 is not used. 很 is usually added and is often weak ('very' is optional in English).

patterns.name: Asking how with 怎么
patterns.explanation: 怎么 before a verb asks how to do something.

examples.english: How do you write this character?
How do you read this character?

patterns.name: Dates
patterns.structure: …月…号 ; 星期一…星期六, 星期天 / 星期日
patterns.explanation: Dates go from big to small. The date can be the whole predicate with no 是.

patterns.name: Go somewhere to do something
patterns.explanation: The two verbs follow in order: first go, then do.

examples.english: I'm going to school to read.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒ qù shāngdiàn mǎi dōngxi.
examples.english: Tomorrow I'll go to the shop to buy things.

patterns.name: Wanting with 想
patterns.explanation: 想 + verb means 'would like to'. Negative: 不想.

examples.english: What would you like to eat?

patterns.name: Measure words
patterns.structure: Number / 这 / 那 + measure word + noun
patterns.explanation: A number or 这/那 needs a measure word before the noun. 二 becomes 两 before measure words (两 is HSK 2).

patterns.name: Prices with 多少钱
patterns.explanation: 多少 asks about any quantity and does not need a measure word before 钱.

patterns.name: Where something is with 在
patterns.explanation: Here 在 is the verb 'to be at'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de māo zài yǐzi xiàmiàn.
examples.english: Your cat is under the chair.

patterns.name: Doing something at a place
patterns.explanation: The place with 在 comes before the verb, not after it.

patterns.name: There is… with 有
patterns.structure: Place + 有 + (number + mw) + thing ; 没有
patterns.explanation: The place comes first. The negative is 没有, never 不有.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu yí ge diànnǎo.
examples.english: There is a computer on the table.
There is tea in the cup.
There are no books on the chair.

patterns.name: Joining nouns with 和
patterns.explanation: 和 joins nouns and pronouns only, not verbs or sentences.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu shū hé diànnǎo.
examples.english: There are books and a computer on the table.

patterns.name: Asking permission with 能
patterns.explanation: 能 means 'can / may' (able or allowed).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ néng kànkan nǐ de shū ma?
examples.english: May I have a look at your book?

patterns.name: Telling the time
patterns.explanation: Hours with 点, minutes with 分.

patterns.name: Time before the verb
patterns.structure: Subject + time + Verb ; Time + Subject + Verb
patterns.explanation: The time word goes before the verb, either before or after the subject.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōngwǔ shí'èr diǎn chī fàn.

examples.hanzi: 下午三点我们去看电影。
examples.pinyin: Xiàwǔ sān diǎn wǒmen qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: At 3pm we're going to see a film.

patterns.name: When… with 的时候 and 前
patterns.structure: Verb phrase + 的时候 ; Time / event + 前
patterns.explanation: …的时候 means 'when…'; …前 means 'before…'.

examples.hanzi: 我在北京的时候，住在朋友家。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài Běijīng de shíhou, zhù zài péngyou jiā.
examples.english: When I was in Beijing, I stayed at a friend's home.
I can come back before Monday.

patterns.name: Asking 'how is it' with 怎么样
patterns.explanation: 怎么样 asks for an opinion or a description.

examples.english: What will the weather be like tomorrow?
Let's go for tea, how about it?

patterns.name: Too / so… with 太…了
patterns.explanation: 太…了 means 'too…' or 'so…!'.

patterns.name: Will probably with 会
patterns.explanation: 会 can also mean something is likely to happen.

patterns.name: Doing right now with 在…呢
patterns.explanation: 在 before a verb shows an action in progress. 呢 at the end can be added.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài xué zuò Zhōngguó cài ne.
examples.english: He's learning to cook Chinese food.

patterns.name: Suggestions with 吧
patterns.explanation: 吧 at the end makes a suggestion or a soft request.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà ba.

patterns.name: To someone with 给
patterns.explanation: 给 + person comes before the verb: 'to / for someone'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ gěi wǒ xiě zì ba.

patterns.name: Completed action with 了
patterns.structure: Verb + 了 (+ amount + object) ; 没 + Verb
patterns.explanation: 了 after the verb shows the action happened. The negative is 没(有) + verb, with no 了.

examples.english: She bought a lot of clothes.
I drank a cup of tea.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ méi kànjiàn nǐ de māo.

patterns.name: All with 都
patterns.explanation: 都 comes after the subject and before the verb.

patterns.name: After… with 后
patterns.explanation: …后 means 'after…'.

examples.english: I'll be back in ten minutes.

examples.pinyin: Chī fàn hòu wǒmen qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: After eating we'll go to a film.

patterns.name: Stressing how / when / where with 是…的
patterns.structure: Subject + 是 + detail + Verb + 的
patterns.explanation: For something that already happened, 是…的 puts the focus on how, when or where it happened.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì zuò fēijī lái de.

examples.hanzi: 你是什么时候来北京的？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì shénme shíhou lái Běijīng de?
examples.english: When did you come to Beijing?

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shì zài dàxué rènshi de.

patterns.name: Years
patterns.structure: Digits read one by one + 年
patterns.explanation: Years are read digit by digit.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì nǎ nián qù Zhōngguó de?
examples.english: Which year did you go to China?

patterns.name: Glad to meet you
patterns.structure: 认识你很高兴 / 很高兴认识你
patterns.explanation: A set phrase when meeting someone.

tone_change_rules.name: Two 3rd tones
tone_change_rules.rule: When two 3rd tones come together, the first is said as a 2nd tone. Pinyin usually still writes both as 3rd tone.
examples: 你好 nǐ hǎo → ní hǎo
很好 hěn hǎo → hén hǎo
我买 wǒ mǎi → wó mǎi
老师好 lǎoshī hǎo (no change: 师 is 1st tone)

tone_change_rules.name: 不 before a 4th tone
tone_change_rules.rule: 不 is bù, but becomes bú before a 4th tone. Pinyin in textbooks writes the change.

tone_change_rules.name: 一 changes tone
tone_change_rules.rule: 一 is yī on its own, in counting and in dates. Before a 4th tone it becomes yí; before 1st, 2nd or 3rd tones it becomes yì.
examples: 一月 yī yuè (date: no change)

tone_change_rules.name: Neutral tone
tone_change_rules.rule: Some syllables lose their tone and are said lightly and briefly: particles, noun suffixes like 子, doubled family words, and the second part of many common words.

spelling_rules.rule: ü is written u after j, q, x and y
spelling_rules.note: After n and l the dots stay: 女 nǚ.

spelling_rules.rule: iou, uei and uen are shortened to iu, ui and un

examples: a or e takes the mark: 好 hǎo, 谢 xiè
in ou the o takes it: 狗 gǒu
otherwise the last vowel: 回 huí, 九 jiǔ

spelling_rules.rule: i, u and ü starting a syllable are written y, w, yu
The apostrophe separates syllables starting with a, o, e
i after z, c, s, zh, ch, sh, r is not the 'ee' sound
The -r ending (儿化) joins onto the syllable before

polyphonic.note: Different characters: only the tone and the 口 radical tell them apart.

readings.use: -r ending: 哪儿, 这儿, 一点儿
noun suffix: 桌子, 椅子, 儿子
changes with the next tone, see rule r3
changes before a 4th tone, see rule r2
